abstract: Markman's secant-sheaf programme proves algebraicity of Weil classes on abelian $2n$-folds once a sheaf on an abelian $n$-fold, with Chern character on a secant line of the spinor variety, is semiregular. It works for genus-three Jacobians. Specializing the Calabi–Yau adjunction between evaluation and trace, we note that on abelian fourfolds the Buchweitz–Flenner map on $\mathrm{Ext}^2$ is the transpose of Hochschild evaluation. This gives a test on the Chern character alone: a simple fully semiregular sheaf satisfies $\chi(F,F)-2+2\,\mathrm{rk}\,c^1\le\mathrm{rk}\,c^2$, with equality for line bundles and the ideal sheaf of a point. The contraction ranks have a Hankel structure in the moments $j!\,\mathrm{ch}_j$. For Markman's imaginary-quadratic secant characters, $\chi=8d^2|c|^2\Theta^4/4!>0$. So on every abelian fourfold, for every ample $\Theta$, no simple sheaf with such a character is fully semiregular, and Perry's $G$-semiregularity for free translation groups does not rescue them. For the weaker condition that Markman's argument actually uses (injectivity on the image of evaluation, i.e. $\ker\mathrm{ob}=\ker\mathrm{ch}$), both of his genus-four families fail as well. They cannot deform to first order transversally to the Jacobian locus: for the theta-divisor sheaves, a non-Cartier surface does not survive the smoothing of the nodes of $\Theta$; for the union ideals, Brill–Noether loci are rigid (Lombardi–Tirabassi). By Künneth the failure lifts to his product objects on $X\times\hat X$, along a direction tangent to the Weil period domain. So the mechanism with Brill–Noether seeds is special to genus three, where the Jacobian locus is open. A variant covers his real-multiplication construction, e.g. for genus-four curves with an automorphism of order five. A second, noncommutative obstruction holds on every principally polarized fourfold: any secant ideal sheaf with a reduced component of codimension at least three, or with two surface components meeting transversally, fails, which also excludes Abel–Prym seeds. No new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: v2 makes the clarifications requested in the v1 acceptance review and adds two results. (1) Theorem A is now stated only for abelian fourfolds (degree N−2 = 2, exactly the degree of the cited identities [3, (5.16), (5.20), (5.23)]); the general-N version is a remark, used only heuristically, and the genus-three control sentence is adjusted. (2) New §6.3 with the deformation-theoretic steps of Theorem E as lemmas: E.1 lifting a projective-dimension-one presentation over a first-order thickening (flatness, Nakayama, local flatness criterion); E.2 the Fitting divisor, Fitt₀ = (θ₀) on U, and its unique extension across the codimension-three curves (depth and local cohomology, torsor comparison, five lemma); E.3 the identification of non-liftability with κ·at_F = ±ob²(κ) (Huybrechts–Thomas), in the same normalization as c² = σ∘ob²; E.4 the Hessian pairing, with the heat-equation constant, Riemann–Kempf identifying H_p with the quadric, Torelli's codifferential identifying T J₄ = ⟨Q⟩^⊥, and independence of θ₁(p) from normalizations. (3) The transversality in Proposition 6.1 is cited (Kleiman 1974). The theorem-proof steps point to the lemmas. References [22], [23] are added. (4) NEW Theorem E′ (§6): Markman's union-ideal sheaves (Ex. 8.2.3), and more generally I_Z(aΘ) with Z a union of generic W₁/W₂ translates and points, also fail restricted semiregularity at the factor level. Proof: a deformation of F along κ ∈ T A₄ ∖ T J₄ gives, via Fitt₁ of the lifted Koszul presentation, a deformation of a W₂ (or W₁) component off finitely many points. It extends across them by Hartogs on the normal bundle, contradicting Lombardi–Tirabassi's Def_ι ≅ Def_C (arXiv 1410.7986, Thm 1.4, Cor. 1.5). The scope statements and the open-regime list are updated accordingly; the product-level question remains open. (5) NEW Theorem F (§6): the product objects G = Φ(F₂⊠F₁)[3] on X×X̂, with F₁ from Theorems E/E′ and any F₂ with ch in Q[θ], satisfy ker ob_G ≠ ker ch(G). Proof: the family X_t×X̂_t over T A₄ is of Weil type (P stays Hodge). Orlov's kernel is relative, and by Künneth ob(κ,κ) = ob_{F₂}(κ)⊗id + id⊗ob_{F₁}(κ), whose second term is nonzero for κ ∉ T J₄. Remarks: consistency with genus three (J₃ open in A₃), and equivariant descent does not help. The scope statements in §1 and §7 are updated: the product-level question for Brill–Noether-built factors is now settled negatively. (6) NEW Corollary F′, conditional: for the real-multiplication setting of Markman arXiv 2509.23079, if the Hilbert modular locus is not tangent to J₄ at X, then E = Φ(F₁⊠F₂^∨) with F₁ from Theorems E/E′ has ker ob_E ≠ ker ch(E) for every F₂ with ch(F₂) ∈ B. So the condition on F₂ alone in his Question 11.2.2 cannot suffice there. The transversality hypothesis reduces to Q ∉ V₁·V₂ for the canonical quadric. A weight argument shows it holds for every non-hyperelliptic genus-four curve with an order-5 automorphism and rational quotient, such as y⁵ = x(x−1)²(x−λ)³ (checked numerically in rm_transversal.py: unique rank-4 quadric ω₁ω₄ − ω₂ω₃). (7) NEW Remark 7.1 (Prym seeds), with prym_seeds.py: on a general ppav4, viewed as a Prym, ideal sheaves of unions of Abel–Prym surfaces, Abel–Prym curves and points have K₀-secant characters. For example m = 0, d = 4: one surface, 7 curves and 12−ε points, where ε = χ(O_S) − 28 ≤ 6 is a correction at the contracted curve: R¹ length ℓ = 5 minus a conductor δ. GRR is calibrated on Markman's W₂. They satisfy the H¹(T)-part of the restricted condition, unlike the Jacobian seeds. Full restricted semiregularity is left open. (8) NEW Theorem G (§6), found independently and slightly earlier by cm_symmetry_scout, who also audited it. On every principally polarized abelian fourfold, an ideal sheaf I_Z⊗L with a K₀-secant character (any d, m) and a reduced component of codimension ≥ 3 fails the restricted condition. The failing direction is a noncommutative one in ker c², which surjects onto H⁰(∧²T) via a 12×12 minor −(d+m²)⁶. Locally, the commutator of lifted generators gives ε·π(dx_i,dx_j) in the deformed ideal, and for codimension ≥ 3, Ext¹(I_W,O) = 0 reduces deformations of I_W to deformations of O_W. This gives a second, Jacobian-independent proof for Markman's Ex. 8.2.3 (all families of Prop. 6.1 contain points or curves), and it excludes the Prym seeds of Remark 7.1, settling that remark negatively. Supporting scripts: kerc2_symbolic.py, kerc2_bivector.py, ext2_codim.sing. Theorem G(ii): two surface components meeting transversally at a point also obstruct. Lifting the linear resolution R(−4) → R(−3)⁴ → R(−2)⁴ of (x₁,x₂)∩(x₃,x₄) over A_ε forces the constant matrix {d₁,d₂}_π to vanish, and its entries are the four mixed components of π; this matches the length-4 local Ext². On a general ppav4 this leaves only seeds of pure dimension 2 with no transversal meeting points. Scripts: resolution_obstruction.py, two_planes_ext.sing.

coauthors.contribution: Theorem G: independent discovery of the local obstruction for point components, extension to curve components, audit of the proof, and the rank computation rk ob² = 18 vs rk c² = 12; audit of the relative-Orlov/Künneth step in Theorem F.

title: A Chern-character test for semiregularity on abelian fourfolds, and the failure of Markman's imaginary-quadratic secant sheaves
